scores.claim_text: PACS operates over 200 (208) post-acute care facilities across nine states (AZ, CA, CO, KY, MO, NV, OH, SC, TX), one of the largest SNF operators in the US by facility count per CMS data.
scores.M_value: total_hits=0 across all filers; no EPA/USAspending/openFDA registry in the M-source catalog covers skilled-nursing facility counts (CMS Care Compare is the canonical registry but is not a catalog hook).
scores.interpretation: No independent registry in the catalog covers SNF facility counts. EDGAR full-text shows 0 external counterparty mentions, expected for a newly-public operator pre-IPO and not a contradiction. Calibration #1 (sector-registry match): no covering registry => UNVERIFIABLE, not severity.

scores.claim_text: As of Dec 31 2023, PACS's average CMS Quality Measures (QM) Star rating across all facilities was 4.1 Stars, versus the industry average of 3.6 Stars.
scores.M_value: total_hits=0; CMS Five-Star/QM ratings are not exposed by any M-source in the catalog.

scores.claim_text: For the years 2023/2022/2021, PACS's average occupancy rate across Mature facilities was 93%/92%/88% vs industry averages of 76%/74%/71%.
scores.M_check: none (no registry covers facility occupancy rates)
scores.M_value: No M-source in the catalog records per-operator SNF occupancy.
scores.interpretation: Occupancy is an internal operating metric with no federal-registry corroboration. Honest UNVERIFIABLE per SCORE RUBRIC; do not manufacture severity.

scores.claim_text: Medicare and Medicaid are PACS's largest sources of revenue, accounting for 38.6% and 37.6% of routine revenue (year ended Dec 31 2023); Medicare program was 39%/48%/44% of net patient & resident revenue for 2023/2022/2021.
scores.M_check: none (CMS reimbursement not exposed at company level by any catalog M-source; usaspending does not capture Medicare/Medicaid claim payments)
scores.M_value: USAspending covers federal contracts/grants, not CMS fee-for-service reimbursement; no catalog source reconstructs payor mix.
scores.interpretation: CMS is the counterparty but Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement to an SNF operator is not captured by USAspending or any catalog registry. Calibration #1 => UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: PACS generated total revenue of $3.1 billion for the year ended Dec 31 2023 (vs $2.4 billion in 2022), with total net income of $112.9 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $237.5 million; audited by Ernst & Young LLP.
scores.M_value: going_concern signal=NO_GOING_CONCERN (0 substantial-doubt matches); auditor signal=CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE (0 Item 4.01 8-Ks, 0 Big-4 resignations, 0 disagreements over 5-yr lookback).
scores.interpretation: The financial-health / audit-integrity registry checks corroborate the absence of distress: no going-concern language and a clean, undisturbed Big-4 (E&Y) audit relationship with no resignations or disagreements. Consistent with a $3.1B-revenue, profitable issuer => PASS.

scores.claim_text: PACS has grown by acquisition, adding operations at 58 facilities (6,744 beds) in 2023, 9 facilities (1,180 beds) in 2022, and the Plum Healthcare Group acquisition (58 facilities, 6,380 SNF beds) in Nov 2021 for $121M; over 195 facilities acquired/integrated to date.
scores.interpretation: UCC proxy tests secured-debt/distress, not M&A occurrence; it shows no lien-distress cluster (consistent with a non-distressed acquirer) but does not affirmatively corroborate the acquisition history or the Plum $121M figure. No catalog registry records SNF asset/operation transfers => UNVERIFIABLE; the clean UCC signal is, at most, weak supporting context, not corroboration.
